Documentation does not alter the controls in the threat model: TB-002 and TB-011, T-053 through T-058, A-015 through A-017, or the T-041 prefix-cache posture. The unchanged base text reaffirms that provider support does not establish deployed backend support, that diagnostics are untrusted and non-authorizing, and that resume grants no local trust. These claims remain consistent with the threat model. Remaining integration question: the actual Swift implementation must really refuse unknown `reasoning` members and treat the summary values as no-ops, or the doc would misstate input validation. That is an input-validation and availability concern at the consumer-to-provider prompt boundary, not a demonstrated regression. Without the source diff it cannot be confirmed, so this is flagged only as a coverage limit.
